compliance.verdict: The item is correct and passes every gate on re-run; the findings are medium/low issues in the project's rules and documentation, mostly outside the item. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates in WSL and got passed=true. The regenerated gates.json is byte-identical to the author's: solvability 10/10, 204 tokens, all 3 variants reach V5, 11 of 11 mutants reach V4 with kill rate 1.0. Running a copy of build.py in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-04/compliance reproduced task.json, reference.grc and all three variants byte for byte. signature_split gives \"test\", so the split rule as written is met. All required fields and their values are correct: licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation (false for a composed chain) and the observation contract. Id, directory and split agree. The canary appears only in task.json. The level is L1 (4 functional blocks, single rate). Every mutation breaks the spec and is valid, every check maps to a spec_property, and the instruction states every number the oracle uses. I could not refute the item's correctness or solvability. Its weaknesses are about compliance and contamination: (F1) adding a Throttle, or putting the add/multiply stages in the order variant v2 uses, gives a twin of this chain that maps to the train split, so the chain-signature split does not keep this item's twins out of training; (F2) gbf-test-11 is a sibling in the same family but has a different cluster_id. Minor issues: a triangle wave with the stated swing passes, so the rms check does not enforce \"sinusoidal\" (F3); some stated requirements are not checked (F4); the Table-5 role-table declaration for Claude-drafted references is missing (F5); and eval plan §6 conflicts with the only-in-task.json canary rule (F6). Probe files are in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-04/compliance/ (p1_double_err, p2_tri). Item directory: C:\\Users\\Lenovo\\Documents\\!MScAC\\2701\\ml_ops_project\\project\\grc-bench\\items\\tier_f\\test\\gbf-test-04.

findings.claim: The item meets the split rule as written: signature_split(reference) is "test". But the chain-signature partition does not keep this item away from its template twins on the training side. Inserting a Throttle, which does not change any sample, or swapping the order of the two constant blocks moves the same task to the train split. Training-side generators that follow the rule may therefore produce this exact task with different numbers.
findings.evidence: I ran compose.signature_split in WSL. The item's signature analog_sig_source_x|blocks_multiply_const_vxx|blocks_add_const_vxx|blocks_file_sink maps to test. The same chain plus a Throttle (…|blocks_add_const_vxx|blocks_throttle2|blocks_file_sink) maps to train. The swapped order analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_const_vxx|blocks_multiply_const_vxx|blocks_file_sink, which is the structure of the item's own accepted variant v2 without its throttle, also maps to train. The compose.py docstring states the aim: "so a test chain is never a template twin of a training chain". This item is a counter-example. In addition, handoff/training_team/flowgraph_seed_split.md allows "hand-written chains" for training and does not mention the signature rule at all. Eval plan §6 says near-twins must be reported separately.
findings.suggested_fix: This cannot be fixed inside the item: with a 35% train share, almost any chain has a train neighbour once a throttle is inserted somewhere. Canonicalise signatures before hashing: drop rate-neutral blocks (blocks_throttle, blocks_throttle2, blocks_head) and put commuting affine stages (multiply_const/add_const) in a canonical order. Then re-split every composed item and rerun build.py so its assert is checked again. Also add the chain-signature rule, with the canonicalisation, to the training-team handoff. Until then, record the train-side twin signatures for this item in review.notes so that eval plan §6 near-twin reporting can flag it.

findings.claim: cluster_id follows the brief's formula ("chain:" + signature), but the schema defines cluster_id as "items that are not independent share a cluster", and eval plan §9 makes the same point. gbf-test-11 is a sibling of this item in the same test split and gets a different cluster, so clustered standard errors treat two template twins as independent. gbf-dev-03 is the same template in dev.
findings.evidence: gbf-test-11 (parameter-tune) is a "DAC test tone": a sinusoid scaled by Multiply Const and lifted by Add Const to "a peak amplitude of 0.35 around a DC level of 0.5 … swing between 0.15 and 0.85", written as float to dac_test_tone.dat, with checks peak_freq, rms, max_abs and mean. gbf-test-04 asks for "a peak amplitude of 0.4 around a DC level of 0.55 (it swings between 0.15 and 0.95)" written to dac_test.dat, with the same four features. gbf-dev-03 is "a unipolar test tone … peak amplitude of 0.35 around a DC level of 0.35" built from Add Const and Multiply Const, again with the same four features. The cluster_ids differ: chain:…multiply_const|add_const|file_sink versus chain:…multiply_const|low_pass_filter|add_const|file_sink. Item text: src/grcbench/common/schemas.py docstring and eval plan §9 line 221.
findings.suggested_fix: Give gbf-test-04 and gbf-test-11 a shared family cluster, such as "family:unipolar-dac-tone" (or a canonical-signature cluster from F1). Alternatively, record in review.notes that they form one question family, so the analysis clusters them together.

findings.claim: The instruction requires a "sinusoidal tone", and spec_properties says the rms check covers "sinusoidal tone level". In practice a triangle wave with the stated swing passes all four checks. The rms rel_tol of 5% does not come from any number in the specification. Because the 0.55 DC level dominates the RMS, a 5% band on the total RMS allows tone amplitudes from about 0.29 to 0.49 on its own.
findings.evidence: Probe ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-04/compliance/p2_tri.grc: a Signal Source with waveform GR_TRI_WAVE, amp 0.8 and offset 0.15 feeding the File Sink dac_test.dat. Running ./gb ladder with the task gave highest_passed V5 and first_failed None: peak_freq 1248.05, mean 0.55024, max_abs 0.95 and rms 0.596741 (expected 0.618466, error -3.5%, inside the 5% band). Arithmetic: with DC exactly 0.55, rms within ±5% allows A in about [0.29, 0.49]. Square-wave mutants are killed only because GNU Radio's square wave is unipolar, which shifts the mean.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not simply tighten rms: rel_tol of about 1.5% would also reject in-spec sines whose DC level is still within the ±0.02 mean tolerance. Either add a shape check that ignores DC (a new oracle feature, such as RMS after removing the mean, or the fraction of AC power within ±25 Hz of 1250 Hz, with a minimum around 0.95), or reword the spec_properties entry so it no longer claims the waveform shape is enforced, and note the gap in review.notes.

findings.claim: The instruction states requirements that the oracle cannot check, and some of the item's own accepted solutions break them. The author's report calls one such answer correct. First, it prescribes the method: "Generate … tone with amplitude 1, scale it by 0.4 and then add a DC offset of 0.55". Variant v1 has no amplitude-1 source and no scaling step. Second, "The flowgraph should run continuously until it is stopped": the author reports that a Head of 48000 items passes and lists it as "plausible correct". Third, "32-bit float samples throughout" is checked only at the sink.
findings.evidence: variants/v1_source_amp_offset.grc sets amp 0.4 and offset 0.55 on the Signal Source and connects it straight to the File Sink. It passes V5, which gates.json confirms. The author report says: "Two plausible correct answers pass: a Head of 48000 items before the sink…". In spec_properties, the requirement to run continuously is reduced to "at least 8192 items delivered". The rule being tested is that every stated behavioural requirement is checked where measurable, with no solution leakage beyond what a user would say. The step-by-step method closely mirrors the reference chain (sig_source, then multiply_const, then add_const).
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe the outcome only ("a 1.25 kHz sinusoidal tone with peak amplitude 0.4 around a DC level of 0.55, i.e. between 0.15 and 0.95") and keep v1 as a variant, or keep the method wording and say in review.notes that the method is advisory. Either drop "run continuously until it is stopped" or record that a Head-bounded answer with at least 8192 items is accepted. Do not describe the Head answer as correct while the instruction says otherwise.

findings.claim: Claude drafted the golden reference and the V5 oracle. Eval plan Table 5 says the Claude family must never draft references. The approved plan (Phase 0, item 1) allows Claude-written golden graphs and oracles only if they "are declared in the role table". No such declaration exists in the repository, and the item's provenance records only drafted_by, without saying whether the reference and oracle (as opposed to only the instruction) were drafted by Claude.
findings.evidence: task.json provenance is {drafted_by: "Claude (Anthropic)", generator: "grcbench Phase 3 authoring"}. A grep of reports/*.md for "role table" and "draft references" finds only reports/labels.md, which says "Claude never drafts references". reports/compliance_review.md, which the plan lists, does not exist. Eval plan §7.3 includes "one closed frontier model" on the panel; if that model is Claude, self-preference applies (§5.1).
findings.suggested_fix: Add the role-table row (eval plan Table 5 / compliance_review.md): Claude drafts Tier-F instructions, golden graphs and oracles, which are gated and team-reviewed, and Claude is not scored on Tier F (or is reported without Claude-drafted items). Optionally add provenance fields such as reference_by and oracle_by to the item.

findings.claim: Eval plan §6 says "Every released file carries a canary string". In this item only task.json carries it. build.py, reference.grc and variants/*.grc are released without a canary. build.py is not shown to models and contains the full instruction and the reference solution as plain text, so if it is scraped alone it cannot be detected.
findings.evidence: grep -rl 011687c9 in the task directory returns only ./task.json. build.py contains INSTRUCTION verbatim and the reference chain builders, but no canary. taskio.save checks only the files passed to it (reference and variants); build.py is written by hand. The authoring brief says "only in task.json", which conflicts with eval plan §6 and with the canary.py docstring.
findings.suggested_fix: This is a team policy decision. Either amend eval plan §6 so that the canary is required only in item records, or add the canary as a comment in build.py, which is not model-visible and not passed through taskio.save, and possibly in gates.json.

item-quality.verdict: The item is mostly sound but needs revisions before acceptance. It is solvable and the numbers and observation point are unambiguous: dac_test.dat, item type float, 48 kHz. Level L1 and family build are correct (4 functional blocks, single-rate). The signature maps to test. build.py regenerates task.json, reference.grc and all variants byte-for-byte, and gates.json shows every gate passed. No valid alternative was wrongly rejected: 6 extra correct answers passed V5 (Vector Source lookup table, Rail clip with sine and phase, complex->real with multiply_const_xx, legacy Throttle and an absolute path, a quoted file-name expression, plus the author's 3 variants). Four findings survive. (F1, medium) A near-twin, gbf-dev-03, is in the dev split, and the reordered add/multiply chain hashes to train, so the order-sensitive signature does not keep this theme out of dev or training. gbf-test-11 and gbf-test-07 share the theme in test under different cluster_ids. (F2, medium) The oracle does not enforce \"sinusoidal\": sawtooth and triangle answers swinging 0.15..0.95 pass, and amplitude errors of about 7.5 % pass when the DC level is shifted to compensate. (F3, low) \"Run continuously\" is unchecked, and the harness's finished_on_its_own flag is racy, so a Head-limited graph passes. (F4, low) The recipe-style instruction is not enforced and conflicts with the accepted variant v1. Scratch evidence is in /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-04/ (WSL).

findings.claim: gbf-test-04 has a near-identical twin in dev (gbf-dev-03), and its template twin can legally be generated for training. The chain signature is order-sensitive, so swapping the Add Const and Multiply Const blocks moves the same theme into another split. This breaks the claim in compose.py that "a test chain is never a template twin of a training chain". Within test, gbf-test-11 (and gbf-test-07) belong to the same question family but have different cluster_ids, so the clustered intervals in eval plan §9 would treat them as independent.
findings.evidence: items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-03 is the same scale-and-offset unipolar tone. Its chain is sig_source -> add_const -> multiply_const -> throttle2 -> file_sink, and its instruction uses nearly the same template: "so the output is a 1.2 kHz tone with a peak amplitude of 0.35 around a DC level of 0.35 (it swings between 0 and 0.7)". gbf-test-04 says "...a peak amplitude of 0.4 around a DC level of 0.55 (it swings between 0.15 and 0.95)". I computed compose.signature_split for the reordered signatures: 'analog_sig_source_x|blocks_add_const_vxx|blocks_multiply_const_vxx|blocks_file_sink' -> train; '...multiply_const|add_const|throttle2|file_sink' -> train; dev-03's order -> dev; and v1's own chain 'analog_sig_source_x|blocks_file_sink' -> dev. A training generator that obeys the rule in compose.py (signature_split == 'train') may therefore emit a unipolar-tone add/multiply task. gbf-test-11 is a DAC test tone of 5.1 kHz, peak 0.35 around DC 0.5, "swing between 0.15 and 0.85", file dac_test_tone.dat. Its cluster is chain:sig|mult|lpf|add|file_sink, while test-04's is chain:sig|mult|add|file_sink. The dev split is used for checkpoint selection (eval plan line 20/44), so a dev twin biases test results.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the theme an order-insensitive cluster key: the sorted multiset of functional block ids, or an explicit theme cluster such as 'theme:tone-scale-dc-offset'. Use it for gbf-test-04, gbf-test-11 and gbf-test-07. Reserve the reordered signatures (sig/add_const/multiply_const/file_sink, with and without throttle2) for test in the split file so training generators cannot produce them. Replace gbf-dev-03 with a different theme, or change this slot's theme. At minimum, extend this item's disjointness line to mention dev-03 and the train-eligible reordered chain.

findings.claim: The oracle is looser than the stated spec. The RMS check (rel_tol 5 %), documented in spec_properties as verifying the "sinusoidal tone level", does not reject non-sinusoidal waveforms. The combined mean and max_abs tolerances let the tone amplitude be off by about 10 % (the minimum of 0.15 is never checked), although the item's tolerance rule says amplitude within ±5 %.
findings.evidence: I ran ./gb ladder with task.json on scratch answers in /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-04/. (1) c1_saw.grc, Signal Source GR_SAW_WAVE with amp 0.8 and offset 0.15, which is not a sinusoid: V5 PASS (peak_freq 1248.05, mean 0.5523, max_abs 0.95, rms 0.5986, -3.2 %). (2) c2_tri.grc, GR_TRI_WAVE with amp 0.8 and offset 0.15: V5 PASS (rms 0.5967, -3.5 %). (3) c7_amp037.grc, a cosine with amp 0.37 and offset 0.565, swinging 0.195..0.935 instead of 0.15..0.95: V5 PASS (mean 0.5653, max_abs 0.935, rms 0.6229). The only mutant targeting the waveform, GR_SQR_WAVE, is killed by the mean check (GNU Radio's square wave is unipolar), not by the waveform check, so mutation testing never exercised this gap. In numpy simulation, sines at the edges of the other tolerances (A 0.42/DC 0.53 and A 0.38/DC 0.57) have rms within -1.7 % and +1.9 %, while the sawtooth and triangle are at -3.5 %.
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten rms to rel_tol 0.02: the reference measures 0.6187 (+0.04 %), sawtooth and triangle are rejected, and edge-of-tolerance sines still pass. Tighten mean and max_abs to tol 0.01 so the implied amplitude (max minus mean) stays within ±5 % of 0.4. Add mutants such as set_param waveform GR_TRI_WAVE with amp 0.8 and offset 0.15 on a v1-style source, so the waveform check is shown to kill. Update the spec_properties wording to match.

findings.claim: The stated requirement "The flowgraph should run continuously until it is stopped" is not checked. A flowgraph that stops itself after 8192 samples passes, and the author's report even lists a Head-limited graph as a "plausible correct answer", which contradicts the instruction. The harness cannot enforce this requirement at present because its finished_on_its_own flag is racy.
findings.evidence: c3_head.grc is the reference chain with blocks_head num_items 8192 before the File Sink. ./gb ladder gives V5 PASS (mean 0.5503, max_abs 0.95, rms 0.6187). Across repeated runs, V4 finished_on_its_own was True for the continuous reference in one run and False for the Head-limited c3 in another, so the flag cannot tell the two apart. spec_properties itself reduces the requirement to "at least 8192 items delivered". The sibling item gbf-dev-01 words the same intent as "do not limit the number of samples".
findings.suggested_fix: Either reword the instruction to what is measured, for example "keep producing samples; do not stop after a fixed number of samples", and record in spec_properties that only ≥ 8192 delivered items is enforced, or add a reliable harness check that the graph is still running when stopped (for example, verify after a short extra wait past liveness) before claiming the property. Do not describe Head-bounded answers as correct in the review notes.

findings.claim: The instruction is a block-by-block recipe that copies the reference chain (amplitude-1 source, then multiply by 0.4, then add 0.55), but the recipe is not a requirement. The item's own accepted variant v1 ignores it (Signal Source amp=0.4, offset=0.55, no scaling or adding stage), so the task mostly tests transcription, and the instruction mixes binding output specs with recipe steps that are never enforced.
findings.evidence: Instruction: "Generate a 1.25 kHz sinusoidal tone with amplitude 1, scale it by 0.4 and then add a DC offset of 0.55". reference.grc is exactly src(freq 1250, amp default 1) -> blocks_multiply_const_vxx 0.4 -> blocks_add_const_vxx 0.55 -> file sink. variants/v1_source_amp_offset.grc does not generate an amplitude-1 tone and does not scale it, yet it is counted as a correct solution. I also confirmed that other non-recipe answers pass: c5_vector_table.grc (Vector Source lookup table) and c4_mult_xx_c2r.grc (complex source -> Complex to Real -> blocks_multiply_const_xx -> Add Const, legacy Throttle, absolute file path).
findings.suggested_fix: State the target output only (a 1.25 kHz sinusoid swinging from 0.15 to 0.95, i.e. DC 0.55 and peak amplitude 0.4, as float samples at 48 kHz into dac_test.dat), or mark the recipe as optional ("for example, scale a unit tone by 0.4 and add 0.55"), so that the instruction and the accepted variants agree.
